title: Carpathian Basin
fact_summary: The lowland ringed by the Carpathian mountains, roughly today's Hungary and its neighbours. Huns, Avars and Hungarians each arrived there from the Eurasian steppes.

claims.text: A 2019 study says that Hun, Avar and conquering Hungarian groups “arrived to the Carpathian Basin from the Eurasian Steppes”.
claims.certainty_reason: This records what the study reports, read in the open copy linked under Sources.

claims.text: A 2022 study from the same group says these groups “arrived in three successive waves in the Carpathian Basin between the 5th and 9th centuries”.
claims.certainty_reason: This records what the study reports, read in the open copy linked under Sources.

claims.text: The 2019 study gives this outline: “Between 400–453 AD the Huns held possession of the region”; “From 568 AD the Avars established an empire in the region lasting nearly for 250 years”; the Hungarians were present “from 862 AD” and “between 895–905 they took full command of the region”.
claims.certainty_reason: One study's summary of the written record. The written sources behind these dates are not cited on this page yet.

claims.text: A study of the Byzantine chapter on the Hungarians dates their settlement in the Carpathian Basin to “between 895 and 900”.
claims.certainty_reason: One tier B study, stated in passing.

contradictions.what_differs: When the Hungarian settlement ended: by 900, or by 905. The two studies may be measuring slightly different things (settling in, or taking full command).

open_questions.text: Which written sources fix the years 862, 895 and 905, and how sure are they?

review.note: Checked by Claude against open copies of every source. Marc spot-checks a sample.
